learning.title: Ticket admission has seven GitHub checks that only a live App can settle
learning.trigger: Before treating ticket automation as accepted against GitHub (G3), or when GitHub changes sub-issue, dependency, event or permission payloads.
learning.mistake: Counting fixture runs as live proof. The fake GitHub (tests/helpers/fake-github-app.ts) serves the shapes the client was written against, so it proves everything Bakery does with those shapes: parsing, readiness, admission, locks, replay, suspension and resume, rotation, failure bounds, the rate-limit wait, authority lost between read and write, and the Viewer rule. It cannot prove that GitHub answers with those shapes, and the seven checks below settle exactly that.
learning.rule: Setup: mint an installation token narrowed the way Bakery narrows it, signing the request with an App JWT: POST https://api.github.com/app/installations/<installation id>/access_tokens with the body {"repository_ids": [<repository id>], "permissions": {"metadata": "read", "issues": "read", "pull_requests": "read"}}. Send every read below with Authorization: Bearer <token>, Accept: application/vnd.github+json and X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10. <repo> is owner/name and <n> an issue number.

Check 1, link counts on the single-issue read: GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<n> for an issue with one sub-issue and one blocker, and for a plain issue with neither. Expect 200 with sub_issues_summary.total 1 and issue_dependencies_summary.total_blocked_by 1 on the first, and both objects present with zero on the second. If either object is absent Bakery reads the count as unknown and answers links_truncated, so a plain issue would never be ready.

Check 2, total_blocked_by counts closed blockers: block issue B by a closed issue A and an open issue C, then GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<B> and GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<B>/dependencies/blocked_by?per_page=100&page=1. Expect total_blocked_by 2 and a list of 2 items that includes A. If only the count leaves out closed blockers, the two disagree and every issue with a closed blocker reads links_truncated. If the list leaves them out too, a blocker closed without a merged pull request would stop blocking unseen.

Check 3, state_reason completed: GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<A> for a blocker closed as completed, one closed a while ago included, and for one closed as not planned. Expect state closed with state_reason completed and not_planned. A null reason on an old completed issue reads as closed_unmerged, which leaves the dependent waiting.

Check 4, closing commit_id on a merge-closed issue: merge a pull request whose body says "Closes #<A>" into the default branch, then GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<A>/events?per_page=100&page=1. Expect a closed event with a non-null commit_id. Then GET /repos/<repo>/commits/<commit_id>/pulls?per_page=100&page=1 must list that pull request with merged_at set and base.ref equal to default_branch of GET /repos/<repo>. Repeat for each merge method the repository allows (merge commit, squash, rebase) and record which ones list the pull request. An issue closed by hand has a null commit_id and reads closed_unmerged.

Check 5, permission sets of the four new endpoints: with the narrowed token above, each of GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by, GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/events, GET /repos/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls and GET /repos/<repo>/collaborators/<login>/permission (a body with permission and user.id) must answer 200. Then mint a token without pull_requests, and one without issues, and record which endpoints fail with 403. The code assumes Issues read for the first two, Pull requests read for the third (the GitHub page also lists Contents read, which Bakery's token does not carry) and Metadata read for the fourth. A 403 on a read the code depends on marks the source auth_required and stops that source's step, while the other sources keep polling; the fix is a wider TICKET_READ_PERMISSIONS in code.

Check 6, per-issue label limit: add labels to one issue with POST /repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/labels until GitHub refuses, and record the count and status. Bakery keeps 50 labels and answers 409 labels_truncated above 50. If GitHub allows more, the single-issue read must still list every label: compare labels there with GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/labels. If the single-issue read lists fewer labels than exist, the guard cannot see the cut and a hold label could be missed; stop and report it.

Check 7, label provenance by a real user: have an allowlisted user with write access apply the request label. GET /repos/<repo>/issues/<n>/events must show a labeled event with that label's name, actor.id and created_at, and GET /repos/<repo>/collaborators/<login>/permission must return the same user id as user.id. Bakery compares those two ids; a mismatch is actor_unverifiable.

verification.requirement: Record the result of each of the seven checks against the G3 gate with the date and the repository used.

learning.boundary: Use a disposable repository that is selected on a connected App installation. Never paste an App key, JWT or token into a ticket, chat or log; write placeholders only.
